title: Complete bounded first-PMT selection
drop_in: Correctness reference for one ray, not a drop-in production propagator or JAX acceleration patch. Assumes an inside-water origin outside every PMT sphere.
code:
def first_pmt(origin, direction, centers, radius, t_exit, chunk=512):
    o = np.asarray(origin, dtype=np.float64)
    d = np.asarray(direction, dtype=np.float64)
    d = d / np.linalg.norm(d)
    best_id, best_t = -1, np.inf
    for start in range(0, len(centers), chunk):
        delta = np.asarray(centers[start:start + chunk]) - o
        projection = delta @ d
        perpendicular = delta - projection[:, None] * d
        disc = radius**2 - np.sum(perpendicular**2, axis=1)
        entry = projection - np.sqrt(np.maximum(disc, 0))
        valid = (disc > 0) & (entry > 0) & (entry <= t_exit)
        bounded = np.where(valid, entry, np.inf)
        local_id = int(np.argmin(bounded))
        if bounded[local_id] < best_t:
            best_id, best_t = start + local_id, bounded[local_id]
    return best_id, best_t
integration: t_exit must be the independently computed finite-cylinder exit along the normalized direction. Chunk over rays as well for bounded production memory. Use the same selected intersection for sensor normal, position, flight time, optical attenuation, and reflection. A complete BVH or volume-grid traversal may replace brute force without changing the invariant.
